title: Where the Blue Devils got to play jazz; Alphonso Trent
summary: Jazz was played at colored places and on holidays; Trent was best for teamwork but the Blue Devils had the best soloists.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: So in effect, you could almost say that playing these gigs, you didn't play much Jazz at all.
No, not too much of it. No. The only time we played much of that Jazz was around the colored places.
What sort of occasions would you be able to play Jazz? What sort of gigs would you get that would enable you to really play that music which the Blue Devils was famous for?

New Year's Eve and Halloween night. And them big football games. They had a big football game come here, with a big colored player, it would be college... They'd have the (?) at the game, and they hired the band. They'd always give us the job if Trent wasn't in town. See, Alphonso Trent was the best colored band down in this part of the country back in them days.
You say they were the best band. Does that mean they had the best instruments, the best uniforms and the best pay? Or does it mean that they also played the best solos and had the best soloists?
No, they didn't have the best solos.
But they had that teamwork together.
Yeah. Teamwork. Yeah, we had the best solos. Lester Young and all those other guys, they was out of sight.
